final_message:
I've calibrated all seven offsets and written them to `params.json`. With these values the simulation matches the reference photos to about 0.1% mismatched pixels, down from 6–7% at the all-zero defaults.

**Final offsets (rad):**

| joint | offset |
|---|---|
| offset_1 | 0.1451 |
| offset_2 | −0.1757 |
| offset_3 | 0.2227 |
| offset_4 | 0.1586 |
| offset_5 | −0.2351 |
| offset_6 | 0.2073 |
| offset_7 | −0.2905 |

**How I got there:**
1. **Coarse search:** I stepped through each joint's full ±0.4 range in 0.05 steps, one joint at a time, three passes, comparing blurred half-resolution renders of all 4 poses × 3 cameras. This found the rough solution (about 0.3, −0.2, 0.1, 0.1, −0.2, 0.3, −0.35).
2. **Refinement:** I then fitted all seven offsets together, first at half resolution, then at full resolution with less blur. The first full-resolution run crept along in tiny steps, so I added a step that tries 3×, 9× and 27× longer moves in the same direction. It then converged within a few iterations.
3. **Result:** The biggest changes during refinement were to joints 1 and 3, and to the wrist joints 5–7. Joints 1 and 3 turn out to trade off against each other, which the one-joint-at-a-time search couldn't resolve.

**Fit quality (sim.py):** mismatch is 0.04–0.18% of pixels in every photo. The mean pixel difference is 1.6–2.1 out of 255, which is about the level of the noise in the reference photos themselves. The leftover mismatch is one-pixel edge speckle; no link or hand position error is visible anymore.

Because the offsets are fitted to four different poses and three camera angles at once, they should carry over to the held-out poses. I stopped the optimizer while it was still making tiny gains, because the fit was already at the noise level and time was nearly up.
